chunks.text: 38-year-old male, Associate Professional or Technician, resident of Yishun, Singapore.
General Anesthesia with Balanced Technique, including Propofol, Remifentanil, and Sevoflurane

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr./Ms. [Last Name]. I'm [Provider's Name], the anesthesiologist who will be taking care of you during your surgery today. I'd like to go over some questions to ensure we provide the best and safest care for you. Is that okay with you?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, sure, doctor. I'm ready.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. Let's start with your medical history. You're having a laparoscopic cholecystectomy today. Can you tell me a bit about your symptoms that led to this surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Ah, yes. I've been having pain on the right side of my belly, especially after eating. Had some scans, and they found gallstones. So, doctor said it's best to remove the gallbladder.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for sharing that. Now, regarding your medications: I see you're on Metformin, Lisinopril, Atorvastatin, and you've stopped Ranitidine. Are there any other medications or supplements you're taking that aren't listed here?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think that's all. I stopped the Ranitidine as per the doctor's advice before the surgery.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Now, about allergies. Your records say 'No known allergies,' but I like to double-check. Have you had any allergic reactions to foods, especially nuts, or any other substances not listed in your records?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Oh, actually, yes. I forgot to mention it before. I'm allergic to nuts. Had a really bad reaction once, like my throat swelled up and everything. That's anaphylaxis, right?

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Yes, that does sound like anaphylaxis. Thank you so much for telling me. We'll make sure to note that in your records and avoid any potential triggers during your care. Are you allergic to anything else, like latex or any medications?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, just the nuts. And I already mentioned the penicillin allergy, right? Got a rash from that once.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Yes, we have that down. Moving on, have you had any previous surgeries or anesthesia? And if so, were there any issues?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I had my appendix out many years ago. No problems with the anesthesia that I remember.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Now, about your current health: you have type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and obesity. How have these been managed lately? Any recent changes or complications?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: My blood sugar and blood pressure have been under control with the medications. I've been trying to lose some weight, but it's tough, lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: I understand. Lastly, have you had anything to eat or drink since midnight? It's important to confirm your NPO status.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I haven't had anything since last night. Followed the instructions given.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. Thank you for going through all this with me. I think we have everything we need. If you have any questions or concerns, feel free to ask.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No questions, doctor. I'm in good hands, I hope.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: You are indeed. We'll take excellent care of you. I'll be speaking with you again before the surgery to confirm a few things and answer any last-minute questions. Take care, and we'll see you in the operating room.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] tube in, grade one view

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] remifentanil bolus twenty micrograms

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] sevoflurane at two percent, increased to two point five due to movement

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:20] hypotension treated with five hundred milliliters fluid bolus

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:40] additional remifentanil two micrograms for tachycardia

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Mmm... I'm feeling a bit groggy, but okay lah. Still sleepy one.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's expected. Can you tell me your pain level on a scale from 1 to 10?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Eh, maybe around 4? Got some pain here, near my tummy, but not too bad.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Alright, we can manage that with medication. Are you feeling nauseous or did you vomit at all?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, no vomiting. But my stomach feels a bit funny, like I might be sick.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Okay, we’ll give you something for that. How’s your breathing? Any shortness of breath or discomfort?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Breathing is okay, but my throat is a bit sore from the tube, I think.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That can happen. Do you remember anything about the surgery or waking up?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Not really, I just remember going to sleep and then waking up here.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That’s normal with general anesthesia. Given your diabetes and high blood pressure, are you feeling any dizziness or unusual symptoms?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No dizziness, but I feel a bit weak. Maybe because I didn’t eat before surgery.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. We’ll monitor your blood sugar and blood pressure closely. Let the nurse know if your pain or nausea gets worse.

38-year-old male undergoing elective Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy with General Anesthesia, now in PACU for recovery.
Patient has a history of Type 2 Diabetes, Hypertension, and Obesity, all under control with Metformin, Lisinopril, and Atorvastatin. Known allergies include Nuts (anaphylaxis) and Penicillin (rash).

Intra-operative course included Propofol, Remifentanil, and Sevoflurane for anesthesia. Experienced hypotension (treated with fluid bolus) and tachycardia (treated with Remifentanil). Endotracheal tube placed with grade one view.

Anticipated issues in PACU include Post-Operative Nausea and Vomiting (PONV), Airway Watch due to Obesity, Glycemic Control Monitoring, Analgesia Management, Hemodynamic Watch, and Allergy Watch for Nuts and Penicillin.
Monitor for PONV, maintain Airway vigilance, closely watch Blood Glucose levels, ensure adequate Analgesia, continue Hemodynamic monitoring, and strictly avoid Nuts and Penicillin in PACU care.
Patient reports feeling groggy and sleepy post-operatively.
Patient reports pain level of 4 out of 10 near the surgical site.
Patient experiences nausea with a sensation of feeling sick but no vomiting.
Patient reports sore throat likely due to intubation.
Patient has no recall of the surgery or immediate post-operative period, consistent with general anesthesia.
Patient denies dizziness but reports feeling weak, possibly due to pre-operative fasting.
Anesthesia management included Propofol, Remifentanil, and Sevoflurane as per the operative plan.
Intra-operative hypotension was treated with a 500 mL fluid bolus.
Patient received additional Remifentanil for tachycardia during the procedure.
